Conversely, a loose match is not a real check that vite runs.\n\nIteration 3:\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - skills/presentation/scripts/detect.mjs:109 Regression in `scriptRunsVite`. The command-position regex `/(^|[;&|]|\\bnpx|\\bexec)\\s*vite(\\s|$)/` only matches `vite` at the start of the script, after `;`, `&` or `|`, or after `npx` or `exec`. Common real build scripts no longer match. Examples: `NODE_ENV=production vite build`, `cross-env FOO=1 vite build`, `pnpm vite build`, `bunx vite build`, `pnpm dlx vite build`, `node_modules/.bin/vite build`, and `tsc -b && FOO=1 vite build`. The old check `/\\bvite\\b/` accepted all of these. With no `vite.config.*` file next to package.json (for example a config in a subfolder, which is the case this fix was meant to cover), `runsVite` is false. `detectAnchors` then reports `build: false` for a valid project. The skill treats the project as unscaffolded and asks for confirmation or re-bootstraps.\n\n━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━\nTotal: 3 fixed, 0 skipped, 0 failed after 3 Stage keys its single motion.div with sceneKey(step), which yields `group:sample#&lt;sceneId&gt;`. All nine steps therefore share one key, so the scene instance stays mounted and only payload.step changes. Identity: ENTITIES and ARROWS in entities.ts own namespaced ids (`htmp:*`). Scene.tsx passes these as the id prop of Box, Label, SymbolChip, Arrow, Frame and Emphasis. Each of those kit nodes forwards id to motion layoutId and data-presentation-id. Continuing entities (Box, Label, SymbolChip, Emphasis and Frame through entityMotion; Arrow through MOTION_LAYOUT) morph with layout transition MOTION_LAYOUT, whose duration is LAYOUT_T = 0.6s, and that path has no delay. Newcomers go through Appear. Appear starts at opacity 0 and fades to 1 with delay ENTER_DELAY, and ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T = 0.6s. That delay sits only on the Appear wrapper&#39;s opacity entry, so the layout motion of continuing entities is not pushed back. Everything inside an Appear wrapper stays invisible until it fades in, so each newcomer&#39;s visible entry starts no earlier than the moment the continuing layout motion ends. In the sample, Scene.wrap puts every entity with since &gt; 1 inside Appear: skill, question, the talk arrow, tray, all three cards, the link arrows and morph chips, ghost, depth, kit, chain/verify/pass, route/modify/edited, and reveal/revealLabel. The tests back this up. primitives.test.tsx asserts that Appear&#39;s delay is at least the Box layout duration and that Box has no initial entry animation. sample.test.tsx asserts that at each step a fresh Appear wrapper mounts for exactly that step&#39;s added entities, and that continuing entities are never re-wrapped. Judge B and Judge C gave pass, and the material bears out their reasoning. Judge A gave fail because htmp:you and htmp:prompt (since: 1) render without Appear. That fact is accurate but does not decide the requirement. The requirement covers a step that introduces a new entity relative to persisting entities, which then animates in after those entities have moved. All nine steps share groupKey &#39;sample&#39;, and every entity stays on screen once it appears (entities.ts: &#39;it stays on screen afterwards&#39;). So you and prompt are part of the opening render and are present on every step. No step transition ever introduces them, and no persisting entities exist for them to wait for. path use different timings, and the timings are the right way round. Continuing entities (Box, Label, SymbolChip, Emphasis and Frame through entityMotion; Arrow through MOTION_LAYOUT) morph with layout transition MOTION_LAYOUT, whose duration is LAYOUT_T = 0.6s, and that path has no delay. Newcomers go through Appear. Appear starts at opacity 0 and fades to 1 with delay ENTER_DELAY, and ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T = 0.6s. That delay sits only on the Appear wrapper&#39;s opacity entry, so the layout motion of continuing entities is not pushed back. Everything inside an Appear wrapper stays invisible until it fades in, so each newcomer&#39;s visible entry starts no earlier than the moment the continuing layout motion ends. In the sample, Scene.wrap puts every entity with since &gt; 1 inside Appear: skill, question, the talk arrow, tray, all three cards, the link arrows and morph chips, ghost, depth, kit, chain/verify/pass, route/modify/edited, and reveal/revealLabel. The tests back this up. primitives.test.tsx asserts that Appear&#39;s delay is at least the Box layout duration and that Box has no initial entry animation. sample.test.tsx asserts that at each step a fresh Appear wrapper mounts for exactly that step&#39;s added entities, and that continuing entities are never re-wrapped. Judge B and Judge C gave pass, and the material bears out their reasoning. Judge A gave fail because htmp:you and htmp:prompt (since: 1) render without Appear. That fact is accurate but does not decide the requirement. The requirement covers a step that introduces a new entity relative to persisting entities, which then animates in after those entities have moved. All nine steps share groupKey &#39;sample&#39;, and every entity stays on screen once it appears (entities.ts: &#39;it stays on screen afterwards&#39;). So you and prompt are part of the opening render and are present on every step. No step transition ever introduces them, and no persisting entities exist for them to wait for. The requirement&#39;s WHEN never arises for these two entities, and every entity that a step transition does introduce enters through the delayed Appear path.","evidence":["src/presentation-kit/constants.ts:5-9,31 — LAYOUT_T = 0.6, ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T, MOTION_LAYOUT = { duration: LAYOUT_T, ease: EASE }.","src/presentation-kit/nodes/shared.ts:24-28 — entityMotion = { layout: true, transition: { layout: MOTION_LAYOUT }, exit }; it has no delay and no initial value, so continuing entities morph straight …","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Appear.tsx:23-24 — initial opacity 0; animate opacity 1 with transition { delay: ENTER_DELAY, duration: ENTER_T }. Continuing entities use entityMotion or MOTION_LAYOUT, a layout transition of LAYOUT_T = 0.6s with no delay. Newcomers wrapped in Appear start at opacity 0 and fade in with delay ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T = 0.6s, and that delay sits only on the Appear wrapper&#39;s opacity entry. On the first loop iteration, i = 0 and the only index check is `now.index !== i` (line 149), so the blank value passes as step 0. The strict string comparison in waitForIndex (line 116) runs only for later steps (line 154). The one call to it before the loop, for step 0 (line 142), has its return value ignored and runs only for the sample when it is not already in browse mode. An empty or whitespace-only value is non-numeric in the plain sense, so this is the coercion the guidance names, and the guidance itself names this scenario. The absent-hook case is handled: a null root gives an index of null, which fails `!== 0`, and `!first.count` (line 139) rejects a missing, zero or NaN count. The e2e tests (tests/e2e/e2e-002-failures.test.ts:91-107) cover a render crash and a transition that does not advance. That signals the Vite server process itself, not only the wrapper. It sends SIGKILL to the group if the leader has not exited after 3s, and awaits the leader&#39;s exit. startPreview also kills the group when the leader exits early, and calls stopPreview on a readiness timeout. In both copies of verify, ensureChromium, startPreview, chromium.launch, rendering and outline checks all run inside a try whose finally closes the browser and awaits stopPreview(preview). That covers success, a failing check, a browser launch failure and any later error. In both copies of inspect, chromium.launch and all capture work sit inside a try whose finally awaits stopPreview(preview). E2E-002&#39;s expectFailure and INT-002&#39;s final test assert that no live process remains in the preview&#39;s process group (groupAlive false) and that its port no longer accepts connections after passing and failing runs. Judge C says cleanup awaits only the npx wrapper&#39;s exit. That is accurate, but it does not decide the requirement. The guidance fails cleanup that kills only the wrapper while the server keeps running, and here the group signal reaches the Vite server directly. The tests also show the whole group gone after each run. So the wrapper-only scenario does not occur, and A and B&#39;s pass holds.","evidence":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs:44-48 spawns npx vite preview with detached:true (own process group); lines 58-72 SIGKILL the group on early exit and call stopPreview on timeout","scripts/lib/preview.mjs:76-93 stopPreview runs killGroup(child,&#39;SIGTERM&#39;) via process.kill(-child.pid), sets a 3s SIGKILL escalation timer, and awaits exit","scripts/verify.mjs:185-210 try { ensureChromium; event, and the tests then assert on exit code, output and the screenshots written. No test calls waitForTimeout, sleeps for a fixed time, or treats an immediate read as a wait. The only direct Playwright use is INT-002&#39;s pixel() helper. It launches Chromium and awaits img.decode() inside page.evaluate before reading pixels, which is a wait on observable state. A grep of tests/ for waitForTimeout, sleep and setTimeout finds only three things. One is the process kill timer in sandbox.ts. Another is a setTimeout inside code a test injects into the scene to raise a fault. The third is a mocked clock in a unit test. Judge C points to the `--settle 2000` test. That value is an argument to the inspect helper&#39;s settle feature, which is the behavior under test. The test does not sleep; it awaits the process&#39;s completion and then asserts on the pixels. bootstrap-template preview helpers spawn `npx vite preview` with detached:true, so the npx leader and the Vite server it spawns share their own process group. stopPreview sends SIGTERM to the whole group with process.kill(-child.pid). That signals the Vite server process itself, not only the wrapper. It sends SIGKILL to the group if the leader has not exited after 3s, and awaits the leader&#39;s exit. startPreview also kills the group when the leader exits early, and calls stopPreview on a readiness timeout. In both copies of verify, ensureChromium, startPreview, chromium.launch, rendering and outline checks all run inside a try whose finally closes the browser and awaits stopPreview(preview). That covers success, a failing check, a browser launch failure and any later error. In both copies of inspect, chromium.launch and all capture work sit inside a try whose finally awaits stopPreview(preview). E2E-002&#39;s expectFailure and INT-002&#39;s final test assert that no live process remains in the preview&#39;s process group (groupAlive false) and that its port no longer accepts connections after passing and failing runs. Judge C says cleanup awaits only the npx wrapper&#39;s exit. That is accurate, but it does not decide the requirement. The guidance fails cleanup that kills only the wrapper while the server keeps running, and here the group signal reaches the Vite server directly. The tests also show the whole group gone after each run. So the wrapper-only scenario does not occur, and A and B&#39;s pass holds.","evidence":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs:44-48 spawns npx vite preview with detached:true (own process group); lines 58-72 SIGKILL the group on early exit and call stopPreview on timeout","scripts/lib/preview.mjs:76-93 stopPreview runs killGroup(child,&#39;SIGTERM&#39;) via process.kill(-child.pid), sets a 3s SIGKILL escalation timer, and awaits exit","scripts/verify.mjs:185-210 try { ensureChromium; Every assertion therefore runs on the final exit code, output and artifacts. No test reads a value that returns immediately as if it had waited. - The `setTimeout` in `run()` is a 300-second kill timeout, not a wait before asserting. - The only browser the tests drive themselves is the INT-002 `pixel()` helper (lines 141-159). It launches Chromium, awaits `img.decode()` inside `page.evaluate` and reads one pixel. That is an auto-waiting promise on the decoded image, not a sleep. - The `setTimeout` in E2E-002 (line 83) is source text injected into the sample to cause a page error. It is not a wait in the test. - Searching the tests/ tree for playwright, chromium, waitForTimeout, sleep( and setTimeout found no other browser driving and no other timer. The unit tests do not launch a browser. Judges A and B said pass, and the quoted material bears out their reasons. Judge C said fail because INT-002 passes `--settle 2000` (line 162). The material does not support that reason. `--settle 2000` is a command-line argument to the inspect helper under test. That test and the `--settle 0` test (lines 168-173) check that the helper&#39;s settle option controls when it captures. The test itself never sleeps: it awaits the subprocess&#39;s close and then decodes the PNGs it wrote. How the helper waits internally (scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs) is not a test&#39;s wait. That test and the `--settle 0` test (lines 168-173) check that the helper&#39;s settle option controls when it captures. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[{"id":"entity-newcomer-after-settle","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"The review guidance says to fail this criterion when any entity the delivered sample introduces has no entry motion at all. It also says to judge every identified entity introduced on a step, by whatever path renders it, and that a delayed kit path most newcomers use does not excuse one with no entry motion. The sample gives htmp:you and htmp:prompt stable ids with since: 1, and its test lists them as step 1&#39;s additions. Scene.tsx&#39;s wrap() passes since=1 entities through without Appear (&#39;The opening entities are rendered bare&#39;). Box and Label spread entityMotion, which has layout and exit settings but no initial or entry animation; the unit test asserts initial is undefined. Stage&#39;s AnimatePresence initial={false} skips the scene wrapper&#39;s opacity fade on first render. So these two entities appear with no entry motion, and the pass verdict fails under the stated guidance.
